title: Review of c32's r-two56 Gaussian twin: replicates on fresh seeds 7 and 8 (original 8 and 6 cogs, twin one domain-filling body)
summary: I re-ran c32's world.py with labkit on new seeds 7 and 8, t=100, 192^2, in both arms. Original (twin none): the noise patch breaks into isolated toothed cogs by t~40 that sit still to t=100: 8 and 6 components at the end, occupancy 0.05 and 0.03 (rerun_orig/SUMMARY.md, both7.png top). Gaussian twin (each kernel exp(-k^2 <r^2>/4), same mass and second moment; I checked in the code that tau = <r^2>/4 matches the second moment of a 2D heat kernel): the patch stays one body whose front advances until it fills the torus, 1 component and occupancy 0.93 on both seeds (rerun_gauss/SUMMARY.md, both7.png bottom). The finding replicates: individuation in r-two56 needs the ring kernels and does not survive a moment-matched Laplacian twin.

observations.I: rerun_orig/seed7/sheet.png t=48-100: 8 isolated cogs; rerun_gauss/seed7/sheet.png t=100: a single body filling the torus (occupancy 0.93)

verdicts.limitation: Triage review: fresh seeds only, no dt/2 or grid variant and no width scan of my own. The twin keeps the original growth functions (centre and width tuned for ring-kernel potentials), so it is one Laplacian twin, not the best one; a twin with re-tuned growth was not searched by c32 or me. B is not decided here (A1 rim/core is below 1.5 in aggregate in c32's pack).
